description: device-sync-hub continues to verify tokens unchanged, and its identity forwarder migrates from REST to the typed Connect client; the live first-run owner-bootstrap flow is proven end-to-end before P1 begins.

requirements.description: The device-sync-hub service must migrate its identity forwarder from the old REST client to the typed Connect client generated from the authenticator's protobuf schemas, with no changes to its local token-verification logic (JWKS-based RS256). The first-run owner-bootstrap flow (initial admin account creation on a fresh deployment) must be proven end-to-end with the new Connect surface before P1 work begins. No compatibility shims are permitted in the authenticator.
requirements.title: Live Consumer Migration: device-sync-hub Connect Client and First-Run Owner Bootstrap

validation.notes: api/internal/token/local_verify_test.go: device-sync-hub's local JWKS verifier (imported or replicated) verifies a token issued by scenario-authenticator without any code change to the verifier

api/handlers/auth/device_sync_hub_e2e_test.go: stand up scenario-authenticator and an in-process device-sync-hub stub using the typed Connect client; perform register → login → receive token → device-sync-hub local-verifies token using JWKS fetched from /.well-known/jwks.json → success

api/handlers/auth/device_sync_hub_e2e_test.go: first-run owner bootstrap — fresh SQLite, call the bootstrap RPC/flow via the Connect client, assert admin account created, admin token issued, device-sync-hub local-verifies the token

api/handlers/session/device_sync_hub_revoke_e2e_test.go: device-sync-hub calls session revoke via the Connect equivalent endpoint; assert session is revoked in Redis and subsequent token use is rejected

bas/integration/device_sync_hub_migration_test: end-to-end browser test simulates first-run setup, confirms owner account creation, and verifies device-sync-hub can authenticate subsequent requests using the new Connect surface
